questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good selection of relevant courses at a recognized university, and of course the Australian lifestyle

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Be aware that University of Sydney emails you a lot of information up front (and its very repetitive so the relevant points often drown). It's helpful if you read all of it. This information can only be found in the emails received so keep them! They don't have a website or anything you can go look at.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails with information and an introductory meeting for all exchange studies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to find housing in Sydney. The quality is very poor (dirt, mould, drafts) and the prices are high. It was easy enough to go on viewings, but there was often 30 people viewing the same room, and the room was not in a liveable condition. Keep away from the large rental companies that posts in facebook groups about rooms in Sydney - you can recognize them by the same person posting lots of different rooms and the posts all have similar wording.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus was definitely worth it, because the student housing is incredibly expensive compared to what you get and the buildings are full of 18 year olds that just started drinking.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sydney has a ridiculous housing situation. Everyone is trying to rip you off and the housing market is one of the most overvalued in the world right now.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was very messy because they kept changing the availability of courses so I had to re-register several times and I didn't end up with the courses I wanted to. You register online but you have to read the instructions carefully because its not obvious how to use the system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could also send you advisor an email or show up at certain locations on campus where they offered pop-up assistance

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. They changed a lot of classes from being offered both in-person and online to only online. A lot of classes were also cancelled last minute. I ended up having some online-only courses because I didn't know what to do. Initially, they offered a wide variety of courses that seemed very interesting, but in the end, the options were disappointingly limited.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think my experience was coloured by this being the first 'in-person' exchange semester after COVID. Hopefully it's not going to be like this in the future, as people return to campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very basic. Don't expect anything to ground-breaking, but you could be lucky of course. However, the workload is high because you are expected to hand in a lot of assignments and engage during the tutorials. I ended up studying a lot more than I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: USYD operated with mandatory tutorials in most classes. The called your name to make sure you were there and you were expected to actively participate and contribute to group discussions. Lectures were much of the same, even though I also had classes that mixed the lecture and tutorial to a large, interactive session.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
US-China Relations
Globalisation and Governance
International Security
Strategy and Security in the Indo-Pacific

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: US-China relations is the only course I would recommend. The lecturer was exceptional and it was very interesting, attempting to look at US-China relations from the perspective of both sides. Workload was very high!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Temporary housing until I found a place to stay ended up being a lot more than I hoped. In general, everything is expensive in Sydney.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables are very expensive..... Housing and other things like internet subscription and SIM cards are very expensive compared to what you get. Gyms are very expensive too!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: During the extensive intro-period we very introduced to everything the University has to offer. Whether it is worth joining any of the clubs and whatever depend on how close you live to the University and how much time you want to spend on campus vs off-campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything! Sports clubs, religious and cultural clubs, everything in-between (e,g, the chocolate society) on-campus bars and concert arenas, lot's of free introductory events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for all events in the introductory period and meet a lot of people! Events often had free drinks, snacks, food and merchandise

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city has so much to offer and I enjoyed the nice coastal walks such as Rose Bay - Hornby Lighthouse, Bondi - Cogee and Spit - Manly. Get out of the city and see the Blue Mountains too

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy to adjust to Australia, but I was surprised by the amount of Asians at the university. There was actually a bit of cultural adjustment to do because the university was tailored more towards its Asian students than Australians. I went to an 'afternoon tea' at my faculty that turned out to be dumplings, spring rolls and sodas which was quite funny. The level of English was also not what I expected, you are apparently allowed to study in English at an English university without knowing English (sometimes they provided Chinese translations or auto-translate the lectures to Chinese). It was very hard to connect with my fellow students because it was difficult to communicate.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Good luck finding them!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australia is not that different

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I got my share of Australian culture off-campus, not on campus. I like how Australians in general are very active people, early risers and enjoy their time outside

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be vigilant when it comes to housing, it's important for whether you get a good stay. Location is important, public transport is fine but Sydney is really huge! 
Don't put too much effort into your assignments, have fun instead!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Time goes fast, plan your travels in advance

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have met a lot of amazing international students that I am looking forward to staying in touch with! Sydney is also such a fun city to stay in

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing in the beginning!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
